name: Standard Chess
desc: Standard FIDE rules

name: King of the Hill
desc: Moving your king to d4/d5/e4/e5 is an instant win.

name: Three-Check
desc: First to check the opponent three times wins.

name: Antichess
desc: Captures are mandatory. First to lose all pieces wins.

name: Racing Kings
desc: No checks allowed. Both kings start on 1st rank. Race to the top.

name: Fischer Random (Chess960)
desc: Back rank pieces randomised (960 positions). Castling rules adapted.

name: Rifle Chess
desc: Capturing pieces stay on their square — they 'shoot' the target.

name: Atomic Chess
desc: Captures cause explosions destroying all pieces on adjacent squares.

name: Marseillais Chess
desc: Each player makes TWO moves per turn (except White's first turn).

name: Duck Chess
desc: After each move, place the duck (blocker) on any empty square.

name: Fog of War Chess
desc: You only see squares your pieces can move to. No check warnings.

name: No Castling Chess
desc: Standard chess with castling removed. Kings must develop naturally.

name: Torpedo Chess
desc: Pawns can move two squares forward from any rank, not just the starting rank.

name: Horde Chess
desc: White has a full army. Black has 36 pawns. Asymmetric survival.

name: Extinction Chess
desc: Lose all your knights, bishops, rooks, or pawns — you lose the game.

name: Maharaja & Sepoys
desc: One player has a full army. The other has one piece that moves as queen + knight.

name: Capablanca Chess
desc: Two extra pieces: Archbishop (B+N) and Chancellor (R+N). Wider board.

name: Grand Chess
desc: Same new pieces as Capablanca, bigger board, pawns start on rank 3.

name: Courier Chess
desc: Medieval German variant from the 1200s. Extra bishops and sage pieces.

name: Breakthrough
desc: Pawns only — first to reach the far side wins. No captures backward.

name: Knightmate
desc: Knight and King swap roles. The Knight is royal; Kings move as knights.

name: Monster Chess
desc: White moves twice per turn but starts with only King, Rooks, and pawns.

name: Progressive
desc: Moves per turn escalate: 1, 2, 3, 4... Check ends your turn early.

name: Chigorin
desc: White's Bishops replaced by Knights. Four Knights vs standard army.

name: Almost Chess
desc: White's Queen is replaced by a Chancellor (Rook + Knight compound).

name: Amazon Chess
desc: Queens replaced by Amazons (Queen + Knight). The most powerful piece possible.

name: Upside-Down
desc: Pieces start on the opponent's back rank. Instant tactical chaos.

name: Single-Check
desc: One check wins. No checkmate needed — any single check ends the game.

name: Five-Check
desc: Extended Three-Check — five checks wins instead of three.

name: Giveaway
desc: Forced captures. King is not royal. Stalemate is a loss.

name: Suicide Chess
desc: Forced captures like Giveaway, but stalemate is a draw, not a loss.

name: Stalemate Wins
desc: Standard chess but stalemate is a win, not a draw.

name: Codrus
desc: No check exists. You win by getting your own King captured.

name: Makpong
desc: King cannot move out of check. You must block or capture instead.

name: Los Alamos
desc: First computer chess (1956). 6x6 board, no Bishops, no castling.

name: Minichess
desc: Gardner's 5x5 board. All piece types, fast tactical games.

name: Endgame Chess
desc: Only Kings and pawns. Pure endgame technique from move one.

name: Peasants' Revolt
desc: White has King + 8 pawns vs Black's King + 2 Knights + 8 pawns.

name: Pawns Only
desc: Kings and pawns only. First to promote wins instantly.
